subject: Implement Initial Slot Processing (#175)
body:
* Implement updateProposerRandaoLayer

* Rename updateProposerRandaoSkips to updateProposerRandaoLayer
* Add validator_registry and shard_committees_at_slots initialization to
the default constructor of BeaconState to enable slot processing action
to be taken when Artemis is ran, without giving an error due to null variables.
* Create a public getBeacon_proposer_index method to BeaconState to be
able to call the method from the StateTransition module.

NOTES:
- I haven't been able to test it yet, due to failure to think of what values
to initialize the validator_registry and shard_committees_at_slots with.
- If UpdateProposerRandaoLayer can become a method of BeaconState
instead of StateTransition, there wouldn't be a public method
implemented for getBeacon_proposer_index. It's private counterpart
get_beacon_proposer_index could be used.

* Remove initiation of variables in constructor

Remove initiation of variables such as shard committees and validator registries
in BeaconState constructor. This will result in a lot of null pointer errors being
thrown when running.

* Ran spotlessApply

* Remove public duplicate function

* Remove getBeacon_proposer_index
* Change get_beacon_proposer_index from private to public

* Refactor local variable name

* Test updateProposerRandaoLayer method

StateTransitionTest file in the process.

* Implement and test updateLatestRandaoMixes

* Refactor state transition tests

* Refactor PR from snake to camel case

* implement get_previous_block_root

* refactor to setPrevious_block_root

* Fix setPrevious_block_root

According to spec previous block root corresponds to slot - 1 (assuming state slot number is updated already)

* Implement updateRecentBlockHashes

* Implement updateBatched_block_roots method in BeaconState in order to
make state changes to BeaconState object inside the class instead of in state transition object(during state transition).
* Make use of a function called merkle_roots in

author: Adrian Sutton
subject: Use EventChannels for deposits (#1124)
body:
Introduces EventChannels which provide largely the same functionality as EventBus but with a few improvements:
 * Events are defined using methods on an interface so it's easy to find where they are published and handled
 * Events are guaranteed to be delivered in the same order that they are published. This includes for different events defined on the same interface.
 * All events from a given interface are processed on one thread per subscriber.
 * Backpressure is applied to publishers when subscribers are unable to keep up. EventBus would just keep creating publishing threads until resource limits were hit.

subject: [#1297] - teku validator register subcommand - use encrypted signing keystore   (#1369)
body:
Introduce additional cli options in `teku validator register` subcommand to allow using BLS keystore for signer private key.
~~~
     --signing-keystore-file=<FILE>
                            Path to the keystore file containing encrypted
                              signing key for the validator
      --signing-keystore-password-env=<ENV_VAR>
                            Read password from environment variable to decrypt
                              the validator keystore
      --signing-keystore-password-file=<FILE>
                            Read password from the file to decrypt the
                              validator keystore
~~~
These cli options are mutually exclusive with `--signing-key`. 

Signed-off-by: Usman Saleem <usman@usmans.info>

author: Anton Nashatyrev
subject: Optimize backing views (#1465)
body:
* read-only views cache their child views so the composite view traverse performance is somewhat near array traverse
* a mutable view has backing immutable view plus changes accumulated in a simple HashMap
* When doing commitChanges the changes accumulated in a mutable view are merged with backing immutable view cache to form the created immutable view cache in place.
* The backing binary tree is built in batched manner: tree nodes updated in a single pass
* The Validator container was made immutable for performance reasons: the changes to Validator is pretty rare comparing to reads.
* Deprecate BeaconState.createWritableCopy() in favor of BeaconState.updated(Consumer<MutableBeaconState>) to restrict the scope of using MutableBeaconState instances and enforce immutable instances usage.
* Pre calculate base_rewards instead of re-calculating them inline
* Lazily calculate PublicKey rawData from point
Co-authored-by: mbaxter <meredith.baxter@consensys.net>

author: Anton Nashatyrev
subject: Add Supranational BLS implementation (#2453)
body:
* Replace BLSPublicKey.isValid() with fromBytesCompressedValidate() method
* Make BLSPublicKey fromBytesCompressed/toBytesCompressed operating with Bytes48 type. SecretKey.toBytes() returns Bytes32
* Rename BLSPublicKey/BLSSignature.from/toBytes() methods to from/toSSZBytes() to be more explicit
* Hide constructors. Make PublicKey and Signature implementations to be lazily evaluated inside corresponding BLS wrappers
* Fix DLL binary attribute
* Validate BlstSignature when creating from bytes
* Add mikuli and blst specific infinity signature tests
* Add BlstPublicKey.fromBytesUncompressed for testing
* For BLSPublicKey/BLSSignature use bytes representation for hashCode() and equals() since we need ability to compare valid (from SSZ standpoint) 'empty' instances, but shouldn't decode them to real instances
* In case of fail fast when deserializing invalid signature bytes, just mark the signature invalid. This is to deal with empty signatures (valid from SSZ perspective)
* Fix reference tests running on Windows
* Add Mikuli fallback when couldn't load Blst
* Move SWIG wrapper to a separate project
* Update license for jblst
* Implement BlstSecretKey.destroy()
* Temporary handling infinite pubkey/signature as a special case until https://github.com/supranational/blst/issues/11 is resolved
* Generate KeyPair from seed in an implementation independent way. Throw exception when instantiating SecretKey from non-valid BLS12381 scalar value
* Make BLSPublicKey.getPublicKey() package private
* Make BLSSignature.getSignature() package private
* Make BlstBLS12381.INSTANCE initialization more reliable and make it as Optional
* Move BLS constants to BLSConstants class. Make a clear separation of BLSPublicKey fromSSZBytes() and fromBytesCompressed() though they are equivalent with current SSZ implementation
* Make a distinction of BLSSignature from/toSSZBytes() and from/toBytesCompressed() though they are equivalent with the current SSZ implementation

author: Paul Harris
subject: Added import and export for slashing protection data. (#2684)
body:
* Added import and export for slashing protection data.

 - teku slashing-protection export --data-path=<PATH> --to=<FILE>

 - teku slashing-protection import --data-path=<PATH> --from=<FILE>

 - --data-path defaults to the default path for teku.

 Exporting will only export to the minimal interchange format, as that is all that's stored by teku.

 On import, complete or minimal files are supported, and summarised for use by teku. If the genesis_validators_root does not match, the process will halt rather than corrupting existing data. If an existing file is found, the MAX of the existing data and imported data will be stored, to ensure there is no possibility of stepping 'backwards' in slashing protection data.

 fixes #2601

Signed-off-by: Paul Harris <paul.harris@consensys.net>

Co-authored-by: Adrian Sutton <adrian@symphonious.net>

subject: If the requested slot is empty, get the block header for the latest block. (#3073)
body:
* If the current slot is empty, get the block header for the latest block.

 - Previously an empty head slot would result in a 404 (not found) error.

 - It was possible for the slot of the finalized epoch to be empty, which would result in 404.

 - Retrieval of a specific slot may now result in a different slot being returned by `/eth/v1/beacon/headers/*` endpoints if the numeric requested slot had no block.

 - An empty slot will have the block header from the most recent block at that point, complete with the slot it was produced for.

 fixes #3071

author: Paul Harris
subject: add a command line interface to send voluntary exits for a validator. (#3196)
body:
The option is hidden,
`teku voluntary-exit --beacon-node-api-endpoint URL --validator-keys KEY:PASS --epoch EPOCH`

The validator key and password file are used to load the validator, so that the exit can be signed.

Care should be taken, if the entire validator keys folder and password folder is passed, exits will be generated for all keys.

If the validation from the remote host fails, the failure message is too generic to be useful currently, so the program only reports that the exit submission failed.

Note: the epoch must be the current or a previous epoch, or a validation error will be received, and the exit won't be processed.

fixes #2461

Signed-off-by: Paul Harris <paul.harris@consensys.net>

author: Adrian Sutton
subject: Avoid BigInteger multiplication when calculating base rewards (#3372)
body:
Previously UInt64.times switched to using BigInteger to perform multiplication when either multiplicand is bigger than the square root of UInt64.MAX_VALUE to provide overflow protection.
Epoch transition multiplies the sum of effective balances by 64 and the effective balances were greater than the square root value, causing the more expensive path to be taken.
Add an additional check that if one multiplicand is 64 or less and the other is less than MAX_VALUE / 64, use the fast path as the result is known to not overflow.

`--ws-checkpoint` now accepts either root:epoch, or a URL containing key `ws_checkpoint` (formatted as root:epoch) as part of a json payload.

If the checkpoint passed starts with '0x', then it will be loaded as a literal checkpoint reference, otherwise it will attempt to load from url.

author: Paul Harris
subject: Update remote validator client to handle altair block creation (#3978)
body:
* Update remote validator client to handle altair block creation

Added a hidden cli option to direct the validator client to use `eth/v2/validator/blocks/:slot`, so that the version field in the response can be used to determine which type of block should be deserialized.

The `eth/v1/validator/blocks/:slot` endpoint does return an altair block but its less simple to decode, which ultimately stopped the remote validator from participating in block production.

The block production v2 endpoint is part of the standard spec, but we need to be careful switching to it, so for now this option is hidden and disabled by default.

For deserialization to work, a custom deserializer has been added for the GetNewBlockResponseV2 object.

it appears theres still functionality broken for remote validators, but this is a good start.

fixes #3974

Signed-off-by: Paul Harris <paul.harris@consensys.net>

author: Paul Harris
subject: CLI to allow conversion between database versions (#4110)
body:
* CLI to allow conversion between database versions

Implemented migrate-data subcommand to create a new database version.

The `--network` context is needed. It's probably easiest to specify `--config-file` as part of the CLI like normal, then execute the migrate-data subcommand, so the path, eth1 contract etc can be read from the config file while the new database is being created.

 - cannot create a database instance of the same type currently.

 - prints status updates every 100k records, and also a count of rows moved for each column.

 - no data validation is performed, byte data is literally copied. This makes the move fairly fast.

 - if an existing beacon.old is found, the program will abort. Beacon.old is theoretically a real database that was working, so removing it might be dangerous.

 - if there's an existing beacon.new, it's cleaned up at the start of the process - this was likely an incomplete conversion.

 - if the subcommand completes successfully, the 'beacon' folder will be the new database type. 'beacon.old' will be the original database, and will need to be manually cleaned up by the user.  It shouldn't be cleaned up until the new database is verified to be ok.

 - the 'beacon' folder is impacted by this subcommand, but other folders (eg. validator are not touched).

fixes #3882

Signed-off-by: Paul Harris <paul.harris@consensys.net>

Co-authored-by: Adrian Sutton <adrian@symphonious.net>

author: Adrian Sutton
subject: Fix gossip validation around a network upgrade (#4317)
body:
Remove get_domain variants that get the fork from the state and explicitly pass in the fork to use instead.
Resolves an issue where attestations (and potentially other types) from after the fork are published by a node that did not follow the fork, but validated against a state from prior to the fork.  The older state may be used either because it is within the look-ahead period for attestation committees or because there were empty slots immediately after the fork epoch. The old state does not contain info on the fork as it only contains previous and current fork info, so the gossiped signature verifies even though it is incorrectly from the old fork.

* Sync committee duties should not perform aggregates if there are no validators active

There were actually 2 duties performed in sync committee, and the previous PR addressed only 1.

Also don't request attestation or block duties if there are no keys, as the result will be empty, and for remote validators that are services, it is just adding to the request count for no value.

fixes #4370

subject: Publish to multiple endpoints for validator duties (#4451)
body:
* Publish to multiple endpoints for validator duties

To improve participation rates in the network, allow multiple endpoints to be configured to send production duties.

The CLI --Xvalidators-publish-to-additional-nodes will allow the user to configure multiple URI's to use to send validator produced items. Each produced object (attestations, aggregations, blocks, contributions, aggregate and proofs) will be sent to all endpoints rather than to just the primary beacon node configured. author: Adrian Sutton
subject: Remove legacy ProtoArraySnapshot (#4682)
body: Quite some time ago, protoarray contents were stored in a single snapshot which could get out of sync with the blocks in Store. We implemented an automatic migration from that system to the new one where they are stored correctly in-sync.  This removes that migration code and the old ProtoArraySnapshot.  Any user still running a version of Teku old enough to have not migrated away from ProtoArraySnapshot storage won't be compatible with Altair and need to resync anyway. author: Adrian Sutton
subject: Reject create block and attestation requests when chain head is optimistic (#4706)
body:
It is not safe for validators to produce blocks on top of or attest to blocks that have only been optimistically synced. So if the referenced block is not fully validated, return a node syncing response rather than creating the block/attestation. Node syncing is used because the execution engine is still syncing and unable to verify the payload.

Since blocks and attestations use the chain head which is normally not optimistic block production and attestation creation can continue while there are some optimistically sync'd blocks, as long as we still have a fully validated block close enough to use as our chain head and build on. If we've optimistically finalized, we will cease block and attestation production.

body:
Avoids pointless generation of beacon states to determine the proposer while we're syncing.
Also avoid preparing payloads when the justified checkpoint is optimistically synced. This indicates that the majority of validators see the chain we've only optimistically verified as valid and would orphan any block we create anyway.

subject: Perform state transition for blocks off the fork choice thread (#4751)
body:
Since state transition does not require a mutable store, it can be performed off the fork choice thread, then once the post-state is complete, adding the block to the store and protoarray can happen on the fork choice thread.

This simplifies execution of post-merge payloads as the executePayload request is sent to the EL from off the fork choice thread and the CL can then wait for a response prior to switching to the fork choice thread. Thus when the EL is online, blocks are imported as valid immediately and optimistic sync is only used when the EL is actually syncing.

subject: Validator id parameters should not be rejected for bytes48 not on g2 curve (#4848)
body:
* Validator id parameters should not be rejected for bytes48 not on g2 curve

If a bytes48 key is provided that can't be validated on the curve, treat it as a missed key, not an invalid request. In a large list of bytes48 a single key will otherwise reject the entire request, where we could instead just process the rest of the request.

Internally we still need to map keys to the curve to be able to search for the key, so for any valid bytes48 we will still end up having to map to the curve to find the key.

0x hex with invalid length will still be rejected as a bad request.

fixes #4787

Users and roles are possible but not implemented in this version, as we're keeping it simple.

The password is read at startup, so changing password would currently require a restart.

subject: Remove EventChannel indirection for time tick events (#5171)
body: Moves control of the TimerService into BeaconChainController so that it can call the onTick method directly rather than going via an event channel. This removes the queue of events and allows the quartz scheduler to manage back pressure if events aren't processed fast enough. It does this by skipping forward, making it less likely (though still possible) for the beacon chain's view of time to fall behind.

subject: Metric to capture current syncing status (#5223)
body:
* Metric to capture current syncing status

The external metrics publishing is looking for a simple 'syncing' flag which we didn't really have a direct mapping for, so this will fill that need.

It should be noted that the console 'syncing' message seems to trigger well before we're actually in syncing mode, so there will be a timing disconnect there, and that's just because of the way console works.

It's also likely that with the granularity of publishing, you may rarely see this say 'syncing', and that's just because usually sync windows are short, and we're only reporting in 1 minute increments to the publisher.

Tested some long sync periods and the metric is updating. The graph in external service is curious when syncing falls out, but overall it's a fair representation, and the data being sent does represent our system status so that's all we can really hope for...

Added a test case to show the desired behavior for this metric.

author: Adrian Sutton
subject: Ensure gossip subscription is started when we begin waiting for EL to sync (#5329)
body:
Previously if the optimistic sync started far enough back that we didn't subscribe to or unsubscribed from gossip, the sync state wouldn't change when the optimistic sync completed until the EL also completed sync. Since the P2P network listens for sync state changes to decide when to subscribe to gossip, Teku didn't subscribe to gossip while waiting for the EL causing to fall behind until long sync kicked in again.

Introducing a new AWAITING_EL sync state ensures a sync state change happens and provides more accurate sync state information for the node to work with.

author: Usman Saleem
subject: Bellatrix fork + External Signer: Send block_header for block sign request (#5354)
body:
For Bellatrix and onward forks, send `block_header` instead of `block` for external signer block signing request (`BLOCK_V2`). `block_header` contains `body_root` instead of complete beacon block `body` which significantly reduces the traffic between Teku and external signer for block signing request.

Either `block_header` or `block` can be used to calculate signing root by the external signer. For backward compatibility with `PHASE0` and `ALTAIR` forks, only `block` is sent; for Bellatrix and later forks, only `block_header` is sent.

author: Adrian Sutton
subject: Add time based tolerance before disconnecting event streams (#5408)
body: Given that huge numbers of attestations are received at once, a strict queue length based limit on event stream subscribers is too strict as there's no chance to serialize and read all those events. With this change, the event queue can exceed the maximum size for up to one second, ensuring there is time for the messages to be sent if the subscriber is reading. If the subscriber is slow the timeout is still hit quickly without too many events backing up and causing memory issues.

author: Paul Harris
subject: RejectedExecution reporting and health effects (#5526)
body:
* RejectedExecution reporting and health effects

 - New metric for rejected execution:
 ```
 # HELP executor_rejected_execution_total Count of rejected executions by task queue
 # TYPE executor_rejected_execution_total counter
 executor_rejected_execution_total{name="p2p",} 12.0
 ```
  this is a counter, so will track from start the number of RejectedExecutionExceptions received.

 - A new counter tracks 10 minutes (5 second polling intervals) of RejectedExecutionExceptions (aggregated across all threads). The counter is pretty generic, it allows to specify the number of polling periods to track, and you'd be responsible for calling 'poll' when the period changes. It's been configured for 120 periods of 5 seconds (10 minutes rolling). The poll function will return the value stored for that period.

 - if the counter is non 0, the GetHealth query will return 503. This means once the first RejectedExecutionException occurs, the health check will start to respond 503. It would take 10 minutes of no RejectedExecutionExceptions for the node to be again marked healthy.

Signed-off-by: Paul Harris <paul.harris@consensys.net>

Any pubkey configured in the validator-proposer-config file will reject 'set' requests, and will not look at runtime configuration, will just use the configuration provided.

author: Adrian Sutton
subject: Verify operation signatures when building blocks (#6122)
body:
Use the fork from the supplied state when validating exit and slashing signatures

This will mean gossip is validated against the current chain head fork rather than the fork scheduled at the time of the slot, matching other client's behaviour.
The signature check when building a block will then use the fork from the block pre-state which ensures the operation is actually valid.

Also updates the reference test executor for operations to check that we include valid operations and exclude invalid ones when creating a block correctly to improve test coverage.

author: Adrian Sutton
subject: Preserve ordering of updates and queries when async IO is enabled (#6198)
body:
Moves storage updates and queries to use the same event channel when async IO is enabled.
This ensures that any query sent to the channel after an update only begins executing after
the update completes. To avoid updates being delayed by queries, the queries are actually
executed on a separate async runner. This means that queries may be delayed by updates but
not the other way around. It avoids the need to try and buffer content to deal with updates
being asynchronous and finalized data being unavailable until the update completes.

Co-authored-by: Lucas Saldanha <lucascrsaldanha@gmail.com>

author: Paul Harris
subject: Reduced time taken to compute expected proposers (#6525)
body:
Tested on a mainnet state upgraded to capella, ran performance benchmarking on the first selection of state which will initially involve rejecting over 100k validators based on the fact they're not containing eth1 withdrawal credentials.

 - only compare credentials once
 - use single byte compare rather than slicing the string
 - don't touch the balance until the validator is known to have eth1 credentials, as that is surprisingly not a cheap operation. This could get flipped in time, but initially no validators are 0 balance and a lot of validators are not eth1 withdrawals.
 - fixed a bug where the entire withdrawals were dumped in a message rather than root.
 - broke out the accesses to balances and validators, further reducing the times


Signed-off-by: Paul Harris <paul.harris@consensys.net>

author: Paul Harris
subject: Adds sync committee metrics (#6891)
body:
`validator_scheduled_sync_committee_duties_current`
This new metric is a visualisation to see how many validators are currently assigned to performing sync committee duties.

There were already metrics showing the attestation duties and block production duties, named in the same way, so this was just filling in the gap, although the other duties are accounted in a slightly different way, as they work differently.

This new metric is effectively the number of validators that you have that are in a sync committee currently.

Also added
`validator_current_sync_committee_last_epoch`, which will be the last epoch of the current sync committee.

This will allow validator maintainers to better determine if they are in a sync committee currently, and when the sync committee will be changing.

Fixes #6270

Signed-off-by: Paul Harris <paul.harris@consensys.net>

subject: Refactor BLS Operation pool for re-use. (#6999)
body:
* Refactor BLS Operation pool for re-use.

Generify the class so that it can be employed by voluntary exit operation pool.

The advantage of this class is that it allows differentiation between locally and remotely submitted operations, which allows us in turn to select preferentially, and potentially in future perform other operations on local objects.

This does substantially increase the potential pool size for voluntary exits, but we can reduce that if we need to.

Partially addresses #6803

author: Paul Harris
subject: Use progressive balances during epoch transition (#7284)
body:
* Use progressive balances during epoch transition

Also cleaned up some of the processing logic, but only very small tweak.

Basically it's cheap to check if a delta is zero, and if it's zero there's no need to adjust balance. This will occur for every exited validator that has 0 balance, and any exited validator outside of any slashing period, so it's actually about 15% of the validator set, at which point it becomes quite worthwhile to check if the delta is zero, as we save a read+write to the balance set.

This is not a huge speed improvement, but it does round out the progressive balances change.

Fixes #6998

Signed-off-by: Paul Harris <paul.harris@consensys.net>

author: Paul Harris
subject: Increased the pending pool size for attestations (#7289)
body:
This pool is used when an attestation is seen for a block we're not yet aware of.

The two main cases this is going to be useful is
 - when we're falling behind and listening to all subnets
 - if clients are attesting on receipt of block

 The pool size, worst case, would need to handle the number of attestations in a slot (all subnets would have to be enabled)

 With 32 slots, there's 32 segments of the validator count, so at 1 million validators, that'd be 31_250 attestations per slot.

 An upcoming testnet will be larger again, will have to re-evaluate if we're hitting the limit at that point, but we're currently hitting the 5k size of this pool on some nodes several times an hour.

 Having some head room on mainnet for a while should give us a good idea of sizing this cache going forward, and it may need to be periodically tweaked.

Signed-off-by: Paul Harris <paul.harris@consensys.net>

author: Paul Harris
subject: Added epoch state cache configuration (#7359)
body:
Now that attestations aren't being validated against states so often, we need a cache closer aligned to what we're doing when we need to regenerate - basically we want to avoid regeneration of state if at all possible.

One epoch transition the finalized and sometimes justified state get read, and were causing regenerations, so adding a cache to handle storing those, but leaving it size 0 by default for now.

The idea would be to have the current state cache reduced significantly in size, potentially to about half an epoch or so, and have an epoch cache with a maximum size over 2, and could probably be below 10 by default.

This would mean the vast majority of the time, no state regeneration is required, and our states in memory can drop to a much lower number than currently stored in memory (32 * 5 max by default currently).

Tested in minimal network, needs to be deployed to a more complex setup to see if it behaves well in a real environment.

Signed-off-by: Paul Harris <paul.harris@consensys.net>

* changed to using map and setting justified and finalized in storeTransactionUpdates.

This should address all of the review feedback, and the cleanups I made while handling less healthy networking conditions.

author: Lucas Saldanha
subject: teku-5930 Make it the default to not sync from Genesis (#7698)
body:
One common issue when starting a new node is start synchronizing from genesis, instead of using checkpoint sync. Not only this takes longer to sync, but is riskier (subject to long-range attacks).

By default, Teku won't allow users to sync from an epoch that is too old (out of the weak subjectivity period). This includes trying to sync from genesis on mainnet.

For most users, the best option to start a new node is to use [`--checkpoint-sync-url`](https://docs.teku.consensys.net/development/get-started/checkpoint-start) pointing to a checkpoint sync endpoint in sync with the network. This is going to start their node from the latest finalized checkpoint.

This PR added a CLI option `--ignore-weak-subjectivity-period-enabled` to allow users to opt-out of this behaviour.

subject: implement getStateForBlockProduction for late block reorg (#7929)
body:
Currently late block reorg is disabled so this defers to `getStateAtSlotExact`

This functionality diverges from `getStateAtSlotExact` with late block reorg, as sometimes the state we're wanting to use is the parent of the head. In this scenario we actually need to check the proposer head, and get the appropriate state based on that instead.

The fallback given all things being equal currently is to call getStateAtSlotExact, which is basically falling back to the old functionality.
 - if late block reorg is disabled
 - if the head root can't be read
 - if the headRoot is the same as the root we're told to use from getProposerHead.

 In late block reorg case where we're using parent, we need to call `regenerateBeaconState` to apply empty slots.

 partially addresses #6595

author: Paul Harris
subject: Exit with clear error messaging on lock file issues (#8036)
body:
* Exit with clear error messaging on lock file issues

 - When a lock file is present and cannot be removed, this enters us into a state where duties will never be loaded or performed.
 - A single lock file from a large set that cannot be removed is sufficient to show this problem

 Lock files are typically created containing the PID, and if we can determine it's safe to clean up, we will do that and not fail, but in some cases the PID is either active, or the lock file may be empty (full file system for example)

 The DSL for AT is a little messy generally, and I did have to change one function name to make it more sensible, but tried to avoid substantial refactoring.

 This is a code 2 exit, which we use to indicate that a user will have to get involved to improve the situation - eg. validator slashing detected will also exit code 2. In this case a service could not bother restarting automatically, as it won't recover without help.

 Added a number of scenarios for the BN, and a scenario to show this specific failure for VC.

 fixes #8024

Signed-off-by: Paul Harris <paul.harris@consensys.net>

author: Paul Harris
subject: Configuration options to improve testing UX (#8058)
body:
With this PR, it is possible to

 - change bearer token to a configured path rather than the generated default, by using `validator-api-bearer-file`. This is a supported option and will be added to documentation.
 - disable our ssl check whenever not using localhost interface. This was always the only secure and sane default, but to improve testing UX it can be beneficial to disable. This will remain undocumented and raise a warning if it's been set.

 As a tester, you would now be able to use
 ```
 --Xvalidator-api-ssl-enabled=false \
 --Xvalidator-api-unsafe-hosts-enabled=true \
 --validator-api-host-allowlist="*"
 ```
 and your node will then allow connections on the validator-api (standard keymanager interface) via non ssl from any host.
 Just to re-iterate, this is not a production configuration, as it would give OPEN access to your keys. Please don't ever use this configuration on mainnet, like... ever... It is very bad to have open access to these keys, but it can make sense in some testing scenarios where there are other factors limiting access to the api.

 The development flags won't be documented, so I've given a more complete definition here. There's also an acceptance test making use of the flags.

fixes #8057

Signed-off-by: Paul Harris <paul.harris@consensys.net>

subject: fixed flaky test (#8348)
body:
Looking at other solutions for this flaky test, it became apparent that the 'problem' is actually our use of system time, and we have a solution for that, but it's a bit more plumbing.

 - built `TimeProvider` into the epoch processor
 - created a static `SystemTimeProvider`
 - fixed test.

 I only built out a copy constructor for Capella epoch processing, which is what we're using in the test.
 It does mean we need to define the time provider in epoch processing, but it's arguably a cleaner solution than using system time natively.

 The magic sauce is using the `StubTimeProvider` in the test, but that took some refactoring.

author: Paul Harris
subject: reverted validatorIndexCache (#8354)
body:
Reverted the changes to validatorIndexCache, we'll have to take a look again for full electra support.

Although the intent was to only index finalized validators, the result was to constantly be doing StateTransitions somehow to get indices, and the outcome was a serious slow down in the important state transitions that happen constantly, so as a starting point, this will put us back to releasable code that will be ok for Deneb.

Before reverting, it seemed to process 1 state transition every 20 seconds or so, and even just rebuilding a handful of states was taking 10 minutes or longer, which is not really going to work in production.

We'll also need to build out testing for this once we re-implement. Archive storage is already slow due to epoch processing, we can't afford to take this kind of increased performance hit.

I'm guessing the tracker may still be part of an eventual solution, haven't removed at this point but i've cleaned it out functionally... i probably need to clean that before any merge...

`BlockProcessorElectra` was changed to not use the cache to find validator index, as it's a simple operation, and it was causing problems.

Signed-off-by: Paul Harris <paul.harris@consensys.net>

author: Paul Harris
subject: change defaults for all-subnets mode (#8387)
body:
* change defaults for all-subnets mode

When we're running in all-subnets mode, there's a number of considerations

 - we basically always recommend increasing queue sizes
 - we could make our lives easier by reducing our peers, given we're on all subnets.

 Added configurations to override only if they're not default values, so this would mean user-configuration will still be preferred ouver either set of our configuration.

 An alternative to this would be always allow 40k max for all queues, which is a smaller change overall, but we'd probably want to still consider peer count defaults for all-subnets. I believe that we should need less peers if we're listening on all subnets.

 Will probably need to test this, may be able to look at our 'correct head' metric to see if all-subnet subscriptions with reduced peers is more effective than current nodes.

Signed-off-by: Paul Harris <paul.harris@consensys.net>

* increase p2p-batch-verify-queue-capacity

Testing showed this could be a problem on a smaller instance.

author: Paul Harris
subject: Eth-Consensus-version header now passed for json block production from VC (#8754)
body:
When producing a block, JSON payloads require the Eth-Consensus-version header.

Generally using SSZ this was correct, but there was no test case for JSON block production, and it wasn't providing the header correctly.

Because probably 99% of our block production is via SSZ, this was not really visible.

This would not be a problem for local BN+VC, but if the teku VC ever falls back to json (or is instructed to produce JSON), block production could potentially fail if the BN is following spec.

Changed an AT to check both SSZ and JSON block production.

fixes #8753

Signed-off-by: Paul Harris <paul.harris@consensys.net>

Added test cases for VC block requests, and added a validation to the Attestation request test. These were the 2 VC cases where we now require that header to be specified or we will fail.

There was another case in DSL for AT, but we'll see those quickly if we use it.

Signed-off-by: Paul Harris <paul.harris@consensys.net>

author: Gabriel Fukushima
subject: Save earliest slot block in a DB variable (#8722)
body:
Adding a variable in the database to store the earliest available block slot which is used when peers request blocks by range. This is a query that can vary in some case and I've seen it causing disconnection in some cases due to multiple requests getting timed out. Changing it to be stored in a variable brings the query to 1 - 2 ms response time. It does add a bit of logic to handle the sync of historical batches and prune which are currently the workflow in the code base that affect that column family.

Signed-off-by: Gabriel Fukushima <gabrielfukushima@gmail.com>

author: Paul Harris
subject: Added a development flag to enable strict config loading (#9449)
body:
Strict loading was the default until yesterday, but it's caused a number of problems because if we push changes too fast etc it causes support issues.

The new default permissive loading would mean that if a passed config file is missing an entry, we default it and print a warning.

This new flag `--Xstartup-strict-config-loader-enabled` defaults to false, but if turned on will revert to failing on startup if a config being loaded doesn't include all of the expected configuration attributes.

We could potentially start using this in AT to specify minimal changes to a configuration for a test, but for now I've left acceptance tests using strict loading.

author: Jeroen Ost
subject: DataColumnSidecars Sampler should sample minimal 8 columns not 4 (#9599)
body:
* DataColumnSidecars Sampler should sample minimal 8 columns not 4
At each slot, a node advertising custody_group_count downloads a minimum of sampling_size = max(SAMPLES_PER_SLOT, custody_group_count) custody groups, selected by groups = get_custody_groups(node_id, sampling_size), to which correspond the columns compute_columns_for_custody_group(group) for group in groups

* Add gossip subscription for samples per slot

* DataColumnSidecarSubnetBackboneSubscriber should look at samplingGroupCount, not custodyGroupCount. If not, it may not be able to retrieve the correct columns because there are not the right peers connected.

subject: Updated computeSubnetForAttestation (#9872)
body:
During non finality it's possible to have long periods without slots, and in these cases we would need to advance the state slot to be able to compute the attestation subnet.

Ordinarily this code will not be in range to be used, but we will need to start computing epochs to ensure we're in range.

This was found by diamond tests scenario nfin-001

This will help with recovery process.

Also changed logging a little for DasSampler to not just ignore timeouts, but currently just logging it explicitly as a warning.

Also removing cancelled downloads from the pending requests map.

The original recovery process had a 5-minute timeout for the downloads portion, we're up to 240s on download timeout after this change by default (from 40s). Having that increase seems to be related to longer range queries and having tons of column downloads in flight.

Further work will be needed to introduce a v2 proposers endpoint that correctly follows the fulu dependent root calculations.

body:
* build: skip CI checks on docs-only changes

Add path-based filtering to five GitHub Actions workflows so that
pushes and PRs touching only non-code files (READMEs, changelogs,
license files, .gitignore, codespell config, spec refs) do not
trigger expensive CI runs.

- ci.yml / codeql.yml: add paths-ignore for *.md, LICENSE*, NOTICE*,
  CHANGELOG*, CODEOWNERS, .gitignore, .gitattributes, .codespell/**,
  specrefs/**, mlc_config.json; workflow_dispatch and scheduled runs
  are unaffected
- check-specrefs.yml: narrow trigger to specrefs/** and build.gradle
- gradle-wrapper-validation.yml: narrow trigger to gradle/wrapper/**,
  gradlew, gradlew.bat
- test-path-check.yml: narrow trigger to **/*.java and
  scripts/testcheck.sh

* codeowners

author: Lucas Saldanha
subject: Fix decoder reuse after dispose in RPC response decoding (#10667)
body:
AbstractByteBufDecoder.decodeOneMessage now returns empty when the
decoder is already closed, preventing access to a released
CompositeByteBuf and avoiding IllegalStateException from a second
complete() call when a single channelRead ByteBuf spans two response
messages.

RpcResponseDecoder.decodeNextResponse now explicitly closes the context,
payload, and error decoders once a message is fully decoded, releasing
their internal buffers promptly and preventing any stale decoder
reference from being reached again.

author: Lucas Saldanha
subject: Trying to fix the most common flaky test failures (#10709)
body:
* Fix peer-startup race in Eth2P2PNetworkFactory

Replace polled peer-count wait with event-driven subscribeConnect wait
plus a symmetric remote-side check, so both ends of the handshake are
observed ready before buildAndStartNetwork() returns. Handle the
already-arrived case with a one-shot streamPeers() sweep after start.

Also remove a duplicate networks.add(network) call.

Fixes the dominant flake on BeaconBlocksByRange/Root, GetMetadata, and
DataColumnSidecarsByRange integration tests, which previously relied on
a one-sided getPeerCount() poll and were amplified by the
disparate-versions fork matrix.

* Fix send-before-upgrade race in OkHttpWebSocketExecutionEngineClient

ensureConnected() previously set the connected flag synchronously after
kicking off the asynchronous OkHttp WebSocket upgrade, so callers could
invoke webSocket.send(...) before the upgrade actually completed. On
Windows CI (slower scheduler, slower loopback) this exposed a real
ordering bug and made OkHttpWebSocketExecutionEngineClientTest flake.

Block ensureConnected() on a per-connection CountDownLatch that
JsonRpcWebSocketListener.onOpen counts down, and only flip the connected
flag from onOpen. handleDisconnect also counts the latch down so an
early server-side close fails fast instead of stalling the caller.

Test-side: bump the per-future get() deadlines to 30s and wait for the
client to observe the disconnect before issuing the reconnect request.

* Force deterministic blob production in Das50PercentRecoveryAcceptanceTest

The recovery test waited for log lines like "Withholding 64
non-custodied sidecars at" and "Rebuilding columns at" that only fire
for blob-bearing blocks, but the stub execution engine defaulted to
producing no blobs. Blob-bearing blocks were therefore statistically
rare and the test routinely hit the 2-minute log-wait timeout.

Parameterise createFuluMinimalConfigBuilder with a blob count and pass
1 from both _whenOnGossip and _whenSyncing so every proposed block
carries a blob, guaranteeing the expected log lines fire.

* Wait one extra epoch for custody-group count log in DasCustodyCountAcceptanceTest

The test waited on "Sampling group count for epoch 1: 10", but that
line is emitted at slot 4 (~8s after genesis on swift) and the cgc
bump to 10 only happens once the validator client's
prepare_beacon_proposer registration reaches the beacon node. Under CI
load the registration sometimes arrived after slot 4, so the line read
"...epoch 1: 4" and the test waited forever for the expected string.

Wait for the same line at epoch 2 instead, giving the genesis
initialisation flow a full epoch to settle. The follow-up API
assertion still verifies the final cgc value.

author: Lucas Saldanha
subject: Speed up CI pipeline (#10711)
body:
* Increase test matrix shards from 8 to 12

The matrix template's static modulo-based sharding produced a 7-minute
skew between the slowest and fastest property-test shards (17 min vs
10 min). The slowest shard gates publishRelease and therefore the
overall pipeline. More shards spread the load and reduce the
per-shard tail, also benefiting unit, integration and acceptance
tests that use the same template.

* Key reference test cache on refTestVersion only

The previous cache key (hashFiles('build.gradle')) busted the
consensus-spec-tests fixture cache on any unrelated build.gradle edit
(dependency bumps, plugin updates, etc.), forcing a fresh download
and expansion of the spec tests on most CI runs.

Derive the cache key from a hash of the `def refTestVersion` line so
the cache invalidates exactly when the spec tests version changes and
stays warm otherwise. Expose the computed key as a job output so the
downstream referenceTests matrix uses the same key.

* Make generateReferenceTestClasses incremental and cacheable

Declare the consensus-spec-tests fixtures directory and the generator
classpath as inputs and the generated_tests directory as the output,
so Gradle can skip the task when none of them have changed. Mark the
outputs as cacheable so the Gradle build cache can reuse a prior run's
generated sources. Drop the unconditional dependsOn(cleanReferenceTestClasses)
in favour of a doFirst that wipes the output directory only when the
task actually re-runs, so stale files for removed fixtures cannot
linger.

In practice the task now reports UP-TO-DATE whenever the reference
test version and the generator code are unchanged, which removes the
~9-minute regeneration+recompile cost from most local and CI builds.

* Enable Gradle build cache

Now that :eth-reference-tests:generateReferenceTestClasses (and any
other task that opts in via outputs.cacheIf { true }) is cacheable,
turn the build cache on so its outputs can be reused across builds.
The gradle/actions/setup-gradle action used in CI persists the Gradle
home between runs, so a cache populated on one CI run is available to
subsequent runs on the same branch.

For other Gradle tasks the build cache is a no-op unless they are
explicitly marked cacheable, so this change cannot regress task
behaviour by itself.

* spotlessApply

author: Paul Harris
subject: Make reorderImports explicit to fix environmental issues (#10897)
body:
**Summary**

Spotless `8.7.0` can produce different Java import-order results depending on the formatter/JDK environment. CI currently passes on Ubuntu with Temurin JDK 25, but local builds on Oracle JDK 25.0.3/macOS fail `spotlessJavaCheck` with import-order violations across existing files.

This PR makes the intended behavior explicit by enabling google-java-format import reordering:

```groovy
googleJavaFormat('1.35.0').reorderImports(true)
```

That is the minimal fix: it preserves the existing checked-in import style, avoids a large formatting-only rewrite, and keeps the Spotless `8.7.0` upgrade.

**Testing**

```bash
./gradlew :data:spotlessJavaCheck -q
./gradlew spotlessCheck -q
```

subject: Tolerate individual malformed ENRs in discv5 (#10941)
body:
* Skip a discv5 peer record that fails address conversion

An out-of-range port in a peer ENR made getTcpAddress throw, and because
convertToDiscoveryPeer is consumed via flatMap the exception aborted the
whole peer-conversion batch. Catch it per record and skip only that record.

* Skip a malformed bootnode ENR instead of failing startup

One un-decodable --p2p-discovery-bootnodes entry threw from the DiscV5Service
constructor, preventing node startup. Parse each bootnode independently and
skip the bad one.

author: Enrico Del Fante
subject: Ssz additional optimizations (#10946)
body:
* Compress zero-padded tree levels into a single spine node

Sparsely populated fixed-limit collections previously materialized one branch node plus one cached root
per zero-padded level above the populated prefix. Represent that chain
with a single ZeroPaddedSpineNode that folds the child root against the
precomputed zero subtree roots, with virtual navigation and update
fallback to regular branch nodes.

author: Gabriel Fukushima
subject: Remove old deposit log fetching (#10937)
body:
* Remove runtime web3j Eth1 deposit-log fetching

Removes the legacy web3j-based Eth1/PoW deposit-log fetching stack and the
now-dead Eth1 provider stack: DepositFetcher, DepositProcessingController,
Eth1DepositManager, Web3jEth1Provider/Web3jInSyncCheck, MinimumGenesisTimeBlockFinder,
TimeBasedEth1HeadTracker, Eth1BlockFetcher, the Eth1Provider decorator stack, and
services/powchain Eth1Providers/Eth1ProviderMonitor.

PowchainService is reduced to loading the finalized deposit-tree snapshot (from the
bundled file or the database) and seeding the deposit provider via
onInitialDepositTreeSnapshot, without any web3j usage. DepositProvider then relies on
that snapshot plus in-protocol (EIP-6110) deposits. Eth1-derived genesis is no longer
supported, so initGenesisHandler now requires an initial anchor state (custom state,
checkpoint sync, or interop) instead of subscribing a GenesisHandler to the Eth1 chain.

Part of #10876.

* remove PowchainService not used anymore

Signed-off-by: Gabriel Fukushima <gabrielfukushima@gmail.com>

* remove PowchainServiceTest

Signed-off-by: Gabriel Fukushima <gabrielfukushima@gmail.com>

* Remove web3j from production code

The Engine API now goes exclusively through ExecutionEngineClientFactory
(OkHttp/IPC), so the web3j JSON-RPC client stack is no longer used at
runtime:

- Remove the web3j client package from ethereum/executionclient along
  with the websocket JWT helper, and drop the org.web3j:core dependency
- Replace the ExecutionWeb3jClientProvider construction in
  ExecutionLayerService with a direct stub-endpoint prefix check
- Reimplement Converter wei/gwei/eth conversions with plain BigDecimal
  instead of org.web3j:utils
- Build the benchmark ObjectMapper the same way as
  AbstractExecutionEngineClient instead of via web3j's factory
- Declare okhttp logging-interceptor and jackson-databind dependencies
  that were previously provided transitively by web3j

web3j remains only in the acceptance-test harness, which uses it to
send signed transactions to Besu.

author: Paul Harris
subject: Add ROCKSDB_TREE as a database version (#10993)
body:
* Add ROCKSDB_TREE as a database version

Add a rocksdb-tree database version, storing tree diffs the same as leveldb, except for rocksdb.

Added a warning about archive-frequency because its doesn't seem to actually store like that.

Added a debug tool to report on the states stored

```
teku --config-file tmp/configs/minimal.yaml debug-tools db get-state-summary

Finalized states: 47
First slot:       0
Last slot:        1008
Hot states:       1
```

The implicit --data-storage-archive-frequency 1 tree selector previously resolved to LEVELDB_TREE (and failed if LevelDB was unavailable); it now resolves to ROCKSDB_TREE. Guards that were LEVELDB_TREE-only (state pruning rejection, GLOAS
  progressive-SSZ skip) are extended to cover both tree formats.

subject: Remove --deposit-snapshot-enabled and bundled deposit tree snapshots (#11068)
body:
* Remove --deposit-snapshot-enabled and bundled deposit tree snapshots

Both --deposit-snapshot-enabled and the hidden --Xdeposit-snapshot became
no-ops once the eth1 deposit-log fetching was removed. Nothing constructs
DepositSnapshotFileLoader or DepositSnapshotStorageLoader any more, so the
bundled snapshots and the configured snapshot paths were never read, and
the DepositStorage pruning the flag gated is only reachable from a deposit
tree that nothing populates.

Remove the options, DepositTreeSnapshotConfiguration, the two snapshot
loaders, the bundled network snapshots and the snapshot update script,
along with the now unused LoadDepositSnapshotResult, ReplayDepositsResult
and deposit snapshot status log messages.

author: Lucas Saldanha
subject: Replace modulo test sharding with timing-based shard planning (#11204)
body:
* Replace modulo test sharding with timing-based shard planning

Modulo-by-name-sort distributes test classes across shards blind to
actual runtime, so a shard that draws several slow classes gates the
whole suite. Add a planShards job that bin-packs classes (LPT greedy)
using per-class timings cached from previous master runs, and have
collate-junit-reports capture/merge those timings after each run.

Applies to unitTests, integrationTests, propertyTests and
acceptanceTests via the shared matrix-tests-template.yml. referenceTests
sharding is untouched (separate implementation, measured gain not
worth it).

* Move test-timing capture out of collate-junit-reports into its own action

collate-junit-reports references dorny/test-reporter and
ctrf-io/github-test-reporter, which are blocked by this org's
action-allowlist policy (confirmed on master baseline runs too, not
caused by this branch). GitHub validates every action referenced
inside a composite action before running any of its steps, so the
whole composite fails at resolution time; continue-on-error at the
call site only masks the failure at the job level; none of the steps,
including the new timing-capture ones, ever actually ran.

Move the cache-restore/compute/cache-save steps into their own
capture-test-timings composite action with no dependency on the
blocked actions, called alongside collate-junit-reports from each
*TestsReport job.

* Give test-timing capture its own job, isolated from collate-junit-reports

Verified on PR 11204: putting capture-test-timings and
collate-junit-reports in the same job still gets the job killed by
the org's action-allowlist policy partway through, even with
continue-on-error and even though capture-test-timings itself
references no disallowed action. The policy is enforced at the job
level (this org's runner resolves every action referenced anywhere in
a job up front, including nested composite actions from later steps),
so a disallowed action anywhere in the job takes the whole job down
regardless of which step is currently running.

Split each suite's *TestsReport job into a *TestsCaptureTimings job
(checkout + capture-test-timings only) and the original *TestsReport
job (checkout + collate-junit-reports, unchanged). Confirmed via cache
API that no test-timing-* cache entry existed after the previous
attempt; this is the actual fix.

author: Lucas Saldanha
subject: Rename test-suite caller job keys to avoid colliding with check names (#11208)
body:
unitTests, integrationTests, propertyTests, and acceptanceTests were
both the job key of the workflow_call node that runs the matrix, and
the display name (via name:) of the separate *TestsResult job that
gates on it. The two never actually collided in the rendered checks
list, since a workflow_call node only ever shows up namespaced by its
child jobs, but reading the YAML source made it look like two jobs
shared one name.

Rename the four workflow_call caller job keys to *TestsSuite, leaving
the *TestsResult jobs' name: overrides untouched since those are the
required branch-protection check names and must stay stable.

author: Lucas Saldanha
subject: Compare gossip payload size against the compressed bound (#11223)
body:
* Compare gossip payload size against the compressed bound

The gossip size gate in GossipHandler runs on message.getData(), which is
the snappy-compressed payload, but Eth2TopicHandler.getMaxMessageSize()
returned MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE, the uncompressed bound from the p2p-interface
spec. Snappy encoding is not canonical, so a spec-valid message can compress
to more than MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE and still be accepted and forwarded by other
clients. Teku rejected those as Invalid before decompressing, which applies
gossipsub's invalid-message-delivery penalty to the honest peer that
forwarded the message.

Return max_compressed_len(MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE) instead, reusing the helper
LibP2PParamsFactory already uses for the transport limit. The uncompressed
bound is still enforced by SnappyPreparedGossipMessage when decompressing.

* Fix stale is_past_slot specref anchor and trim changelog entry

author: Lucas Saldanha
subject: Reject UInt64.MAX_VALUE attestation epochs from the beacon node (#11318)
body:
* Reject UInt64.MAX_VALUE attestation epochs from the beacon node

A beacon node is untrusted per spec. Attestation source/target epochs
equal to UInt64.MAX_VALUE were signed without complaint and could later
collide with the slashing-protection "never signed" sentinel on reload.
Reject that value before it is ever signed.

* Exclude UInt64.MAX_VALUE epochs from EIP-3076 slashing-protection import

The interchange importer took the max of imported source/target epochs
without excluding UInt64.MAX_VALUE, so an imported file could persist
that sentinel value as a signing-protection floor via the same path
that produces the collision with "never signed" on reload. This
bypassed the guard added for the live beacon-node signing path.

author: Dmitrii Shmatko
subject: FCR optimization part2:  Reuse cached checkpoint states and parallelize fast confirmation scoring (#11214)
body:
* Reuse cached checkpoint states and parallelize fast confirmation scoring

    Load the pulled-up head state through the store's checkpoint-state
    cache instead of replaying the epoch transition, read a flat
    zeroed-balances list instead of materializing validators, resolve each
    distinct latest message once, and chunk the vote scan across the common
    pool. Prefetch the next epoch's balance source off the critical path at
    epoch boundaries.

subject: Stop rejecting slashings for offences in an earlier fork at the gossip topic layer (#11393)
body:
* Stop rejecting slashings for offences in an earlier fork at the gossip topic layer

The topic handler's milestone check derived an epoch from the offending
slot and rejected the slashing when it fell in a different fork than the
topic. The spec's gossip rules for proposer_slashing and attester_slashing
have no such condition: validity is checked against the head state, and
get_domain uses the fork's previous version for epochs before the fork
epoch, so a slashing for an offence in the previous fork is valid after a
fork boundary.

Disable the fork check for both slashing topics, as already done for BLS
to execution changes, and leave validation to the slashing validators.

author: Lucas Saldanha
subject: Decode gossip messages on the async runner instead of the gossipsub thread (#11447)
body:
* Decode gossip messages on the async runner instead of the gossipsub thread

Eth2TopicHandler.handleMessage ran SSZ decoding inline on the caller's
thread. In jvm-libp2p that caller is the single gossipsub event thread, so
decoding a large block (about 84 ms for a 10 MiB Gloas block) stalled every
peer's RPCs, control messages, heartbeat and our own publishes for the
duration. Decoded messages were then held as full SSZ trees while they
waited in the shared p2p queue.

Move the decode and fork check into the asyncRunner task so the gossipsub
thread only enqueues, and messages wait in the queue as compressed bytes.
Also make SnappyPreparedGossipMessage.getDecodedMessage() reuse the payload
already uncompressed for the message id instead of uncompressing again.

Split out of #11359.

* Comments and spotless

- block includes builder_index and block_hash from the block's signed

author: Enrico Del Fante
subject: Report payload reorgs and payload statuses in reorg events (#11437)
body:
From Gloas the fork-choice head is a (block root, payload status) node, so
the head can change without any block leaving the canonical chain: the
payload of the head block becomes non-canonical (FULL to EMPTY). Such a
payload reorg produced no ReorgContext at all, so nothing was logged.

RecentChainData is now the single authority on reorgs:
- a payload reorg (same head root, FULL to EMPTY) emits a ReorgContext and
  increments the new payload_reorgs_total counter
- a block reorg additionally carries the old head payload status, both
  execution block hashes and the common ancestor payload status along each
  branch, resolved with the payload-status-aware ancestry (get_ancestor)

ReorgContext is converted to a record and the two kinds are told apart by
content: in a payload reorg the old head is the common ancestor, which never
holds for a block reorg. Pools, light client pruning and the chain_reorg SSE
event act on block reorgs only; a payload reorg is still reported through
head_v2.

The event log distinguishes the two and annotates block reorgs with payload
statuses when available:

  Reorg Event *** New Head: ... [EMPTY], Previous Head: ... [FULL], Common Ancestor: ... [FULL -> EMPTY]
  Reorg Event *** Payload Reorg, Head: ..., Previous Execution Head: ..., New Execution Head: ...

Pre-Gloas output is unchanged. EMPTY to FULL is the payload arriving after
the block and is intentionally not reported as a reorg.

Fixes #10670

subject: Resolve discovered peer addresses against both local transports (#11464)
body:
A node with TCP disabled built TCP addresses for peers that advertise no
QUIC endpoint and attached a TCP fallback after a failed QUIC dial. Both
fail immediately, waste a selection slot and put the peer in the dial
cooldown.

Pass the TCP flag from the network builder into address creation, so a
discovered peer resolves to QUIC when both sides have it, otherwise TCP
when both sides have it, otherwise no address. Drop candidates with no
dialable address before selection and count them in the new
peer_candidate_count_total metric.

Co-authored-by: Lucas Saldanha <lucas.saldanha@consensys.net>

author: Enrico Del Fante
subject: Keep block reorgs over payload reorgs when coalescing head events (#11460)
body:
* Keep block reorgs over payload reorgs when coalescing head events

While syncing, CoalescingChainHeadChannel delivers only the last head
update and keeps the reorg context with the earliest common ancestor. That
rule predates payload reorgs (#11437) and assumed every context was a block
reorg. A payload reorg's common ancestor is its own head, so an early FULL
to EMPTY flip could outrank a later block reorg forking above it. The
flushed event then read as a payload reorg and pools, light client pruning
and the chain_reorg event skipped the real block reorg.

Make the merge kind-aware: a block reorg always replaces a pending payload
reorg and is never displaced by one; between block reorgs the earliest
common ancestor still wins; between payload reorgs the latest wins. A
payload reorg displaced this way is not logged once syncing completes, the
delivered payload status still reflects the final head.

* Clarify coalescing Javadoc and tighten mixed reorg coalescing tests

Coalesced head events are delivered without logging, so the merge rule
Javadoc no longer motivates keeping a payload reorg by logging: no consumer
acts on one, it is kept only while no block reorg is pending.

The mixed-kind coalescing tests now assert the delivered slot, block root
and payload status as well as the retained context, and a test covers a
pending block reorg being replaced by one with an earlier common ancestor.

author: Paul Harris
subject: Verify block signatures before saving blocks for future processing (#11438)
body:
* Verify block signatures before saving blocks for future processing

Gossip blocks from a future slot, or whose parent is not yet known, are
saved for future processing before their proposer signature is
checked. Any peer could fill the future and pending block pools with
blocks nobody signed, without any penalty to its peer score.

Before saving such a block, BlockGossipValidator now verifies its
proposer signature:
- Valid signature: saved for future processing, as before.
- Invalid signature: rejected, so it is not queued and the sending peer
  is penalised.
- Proposer index not in the finalized state: ignored and not queued.
  It is not rejected, because our view of finality may lag the network
  and the validator may have been activated since.

The parent state isn't available at this point, so the proposer's
pubkey is taken from the latest finalized state and the signing domain
from the fork schedule for the block's epoch. Both are the same on
every branch, so the result does not depend on which branch the block
is on. Whether the block was proposed by the expected proposer is still
checked once its parent is known.

For Gloas, the existing signature check now runs before the check on
the execution payload bid's parent, which can also save a block for
future processing, so only correctly signed blocks wait for their
parent's payload.

This follows the existing signature check for future-slot attestations
in AttestationValidator, and is similar to Prysm, which verifies the
proposer signature before queueing blocks with an unknown parent.

Testing:
- New BlockGossipValidatorTest cases: future-slot and unknown-parent
  blocks with invalid signatures are rejected, an unknown proposer
  index is ignored, a block in the first epoch of a new fork verifies
  with that fork's domain, and a Gloas block waiting on its parent's
  payload is rejected for an invalid signature.
- New BlockManagerTest case: a rejected future block is not queued.
- Reference tests pass, including all gossip beacon_block cases. Their
  future-slot and unknown-parent blocks are correctly signed and are
  still ignored.
- Ran on mainnet (about 13 hours) and hoodi, with gossip reject logging
  enabled. 14 blocks arrived before their parent, during catch-up after
  a restart and during normal operation. All passed the signature
  check, were saved for future processing and later imported. No block
  was rejected.

* Reject parked blocks whose proposer index is beyond the head state

A future-slot or unknown-parent block whose proposer index is not in the
finalized state was ignored without penalty, so the signature check
could be bypassed for free. Reject it when the head state doesn't have
the index either, since such an index can't belong to a proposer on any
branch we follow. Keep ignoring indices that are in the head state but
not yet finalized.

* Match Prysm for parked blocks with an unfinalized or unknown proposer index

For a future-slot or unknown-parent block whose proposer index is not in
the finalized state:
- If the head state has the index, verify the signature against the
  head-state pubkey, rejecting an invalid signature and saving a valid
  block for future processing, instead of ignoring it.
- If the head state doesn't have the index either, ignore the block
  instead of rejecting it.

This mirrors Prysm's verifyPendingBlockSignature.

author: Enrico Del Fante
subject: Read SSZ byte lists in bulk instead of one element per tree walk (#11485)
body:
SszByteList.getBytes() (and the SszByteListImpl override) fetched every
byte through getElement(), walking the backing tree once per byte. The
SSZ encoding of a byte list is exactly its content, so delegate to
sszSerialize(), which copies whole leaf chunks.

Progressive lists serialized packed primitives with a root-to-leaf get()
per chunk; replace that with a single in-order leaf traversal from the
first to the last chunk, which also speeds up every other progressive
primitive list.

Profiling a Gloas node showed the per-byte path dominating
ExecutionPayloadBlockHashCalculator during historical backfill
(transactions and block access list). First-call getBytes() on a 1 MiB
list drops from ~10 ms to ~0.5 ms for regular lists and from ~15 ms to
~0.55 ms for progressive lists.

body:
The initial local record always carried the TCP port, while the address-update handler already omitted it when TCP is disabled, so a QUIC-only node advertised a port nothing listens on. Use the discovery 26.10.0 builder overload with an optional TCP port in both the single-stack and dual-stack branches.

Must not ship before a release that accepts TCP-less records (#11432) is widely deployed; targeted at the Gloas release.

Fixes #11454

author: Enrico Del Fante
subject: Resend forkChoiceUpdated when a reused block production result failed (#11491)
body:
A block production request that reuses a ForkChoiceUpdateData whose
forkChoiceUpdated already failed (EL error or timeout) got the original
failure back on every attempt: the resend guard suppressed a new fcU and
the failed future was never replaced, so the proposal was missed.

Treat a failed reused fcU like one that returned no payloadId, so the
existing single retry sends a fresh forkChoiceUpdated. Skip resending
reused data whose result is already known, since that could only be a
duplicate fcU whose outcome is dropped.

author: Paul Harris
subject: Bound memory held by gossip blocks waiting for validation (#11503)
body:
* Bound memory held by gossip blocks waiting for validation

Gossip messages keep their uncompressed payload after the message id is
computed, and wait in the shared P2P queue, which is only bounded by
its number of tasks. Large blocks could hold several MiB each while
queued, and every block was hashed under a lock before the future slot
check.

- Keep only the compressed payload, plus the size and first 128 bytes
  of the uncompressed payload, once the message id is computed. The
  payload is uncompressed again when the message is decoded.
- Limit the total uncompressed size of beacon_block messages queued or
  being validated to 4 x MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE, ignoring any message over
  the limit before it is queued.
- Ignore beacon_block messages more than FUTURE_SLOT_TOLERANCE slots in
  the future before decoding them, reading the slot from its fixed
  position in the SSZ bytes.
- In BlockGossipValidator, ignore blocks too far in the future before
  the equivocation check, and compute the block root outside the lock.

* Add changelog entry

* Simplify the gossip in-flight limit and far-future checks

- Use GossipInFlightLimiter.UNLIMITED instead of an optional limiter,

subject: Verify validator deposit signatures lazily at Gloas builder onboarding (#11511)
body:
* Verify validator deposit signatures lazily at Gloas builder onboarding

Onboarding builders from pending deposits at the Gloas fork verified the
signature of every queued deposit without builder credentials, so it
could later answer is_pending_validator for a builder deposit with the
same pubkey. With a large deposit queue this dominated the upgrade:
about 6.8 s for 10k new-validator deposits.

Record those deposits per pubkey instead and verify them only when a
builder deposit asks about that pubkey, each deposit at most once. The
answer is the same as before, since only deposits queued ahead of the
builder deposit are considered, and the order of the remaining queue is
unchanged. The same 10k case now takes about 81 ms.

author: Paul Harris
subject: Set Gloas attestation index from fork choice payload status (#11498)
body:
* Set Gloas attestation index from fork choice payload status

The Gloas validator spec sets attestation data.index from the payload
status of the attested block in the validator's fork choice: 0 when
EMPTY, 1 when FULL (and always 0 for a block in the current slot).

Attestation production used whether the payload had been received and
verified locally, so it voted 1 when the payload was verified but fork
choice had chosen the EMPTY variant (e.g. PTC voted it not timely or not
available).

Select the head node, including its payload variant, from fork choice
and pass it to computeCommitteeIndexForAttestation. When attesting to an
earlier slot, keep the variant chosen by the canonical descendant via
getAncestorNodeData. Pre-Gloas attestation production is unchanged.

Ported from the attestation part of #11396 on heze-devnet-2.

* Address review of Gloas attestation index change

- Return no attestation data instead of failing when the requested slot
  is older than the fork choice anchor, so the endpoint answers 404 as
  before rather than 500.
- Use 0 with a warning for an unexpected PENDING head instead of failing
  the attestation duty; detect pre-Gloas blocks from the block body.
- Drop the root-equality check that cannot fail.
- Load the attested block and state with a single
  retrieveBlockAndState call.
- Make ChainUpdater.updateBestBlock select the FULL or EMPTY variant for
  Gloas blocks, so tests see the same kind of head as production, and
  drop the integration test workaround.
- Add direct FULL, EMPTY and same-slot cases for the index rule and
  assert the same-slot index in the integration test.
- Document isPayloadVerified as the is_payload_verified spec mapping.

* Set EMPTY head explicitly in envelopes-by-range test

ChainUpdater.updateBestBlock now selects the FULL variant when the
payload is stored, so the test sets the EMPTY variant it relies on
rather than depending on a PENDING head.

author: Paul Harris
subject: Make batch gather window test independent of submission timing (#11550)
body:
waitForBatch_gathersTasksArrivingWithinTheGatherWindow used a 500ms
gather window with the default target size, so the batch only reached
three tasks if the test thread signed and submitted two more within
500ms. On a slow CI runner the window closed first and the batch held a
single task.

Use a 10s window with a target size of three, so the gather can only
end by reaching the target. The test now submits the late tasks one at
a time and checks the batch is still open after the first one is taken,
so it still covers gathering across several arrivals rather than a
single drain.

Also relax the elapsed-time bounds in the legacy and clamped-target
tests from 1s to 5s. They only need to show the 10s window was not
waited out, and 5s matches the bound used by the other gather tests.

Route them through the AsyncBLSSignatureVerifier, as attestations and sync committee messages already are, so that in production they are batch-verified by the gossip signature verification service.

author: Enrico Del Fante
subject: Seed the Gloas genesis execution payload only for a genesis anchor committing to it (#11543)
body:
applyGenesisExecutionPayloadForGloas ran on every startup, keyed the
synthetic envelope by the best block root and used a zero parent hash.
After a restart the head is already selected, so the envelope
overwrote the head's real blinded envelope; checkpoint-state starts
marked the anchor FULL with the parent's hash; and the zero parent hash
failed the blinded envelope validation against the genesis bid on every
store rebuild, so a Gloas-genesis node restarting while the genesis
block was still hot could not start.

Seed only while the finalized anchor is the genesis block and no
payload is cached for it, key the envelope by the anchor root, and
mirror the genesis bid's parent block hash and gas limit so the
persisted envelope validates on rebuild. Skip seeding entirely when the
genesis bid does not commit to the EL genesis block, which is the
pyspec and eth-beacon-genesis convention: there the genesis block is
EMPTY and children need no genesis payload. Teku's own GenesisGenerator
convention, where the bid block hash is the EL hash, keeps the FULL
seeding.

author: Enrico Del Fante
subject: Key the gossip seen cache by a cheap SHA-256 fast id (#11549)
body:
* Key the gossip seen cache by a cheap SHA-256 fast id

The seen cache's fast id wrapped the message digest in a tuweni Bytes, whose
hashCode and equals walk the 32 bytes one virtual call at a time. The lookup
runs for every inbound copy of every message on the single gossip event
thread, against a map holding every message seen within the seen TTL.

FastMessageId caches the hash taken from the first four digest bytes, compares
with Arrays.equals and is Comparable so treeified HashMap bins stay
logarithmic. Digest and seen-cache semantics are unchanged.

* Add changelog entry for the gossip seen-cache fast id

* Address review on the gossip seen-cache fast id

Document that treeified HashMap bins ordered through Comparable are the
defence against hash-bucket flooding, not the digest; derive the hash with
Ints.fromByteArray; assert the unseen case directly instead of waiting; drop
the redundant jmh dependencies and register the jmh sources for the IDE; fill
only the structure each benchmark probes.

author: Enrico Del Fante
subject: Make the Gloas genesis block EMPTY and drop the synthetic genesis payload (#11557)
body:
Teku's GenesisGenerator set the genesis execution payload bid's block_hash
to the EL genesis hash, which made the genesis block FULL: the slot-1 block
built on FULL(genesis) and could only be imported once a payload for
genesis was known, so ForkChoice seeded a synthetic genesis envelope at
every startup. The consensus-specs genesis helper and eth-beacon-genesis
(Kurtosis) leave that block_hash zero: the genesis block is EMPTY, the
slot-1 block builds on EMPTY(genesis) whose execution hash is the EL
genesis hash, and no genesis payload is ever needed.

Follow that layout. The genesis bid now commits to no payload, and
applyGenesisExecutionPayloadForGloas and its callers are removed. One of
those callers was GenesisHandler, the deposit-log genesis path that has
had no production caller since the deposit log fetching was removed
(#10937); it is deleted together with its test and the ethereum:pow:api
dependency only it used in the module. Teku-generated Gloas genesis
states are now interchangeable with those produced for Kurtosis. Genesis
states and databases written by earlier Teku versions use the old layout
and must be regenerated: a node started on one is refused at startup with
a message saying so, instead of never importing the slot-1 block.
BuilderBidValidator no longer treats a zero parent bid block hash as a
payload a bid can extend. The state-side test behind both checks is the
spec's is_parent_block_full, added to MiscHelpersGloas and used by the
withdrawals processing as well.

Test fixtures build on the EMPTY variant when the parent bid commits to
no payload. New tests cover a slot-1 import on a fresh Gloas genesis
without any genesis payload, a restart while the genesis block is still
hot, the zero attestation payload index for genesis targets, the startup
check and the bid validator guard.

Fixes #11545
