author: Paul Harris
subject: Keep imported slashing protection from being overwritten by cache (#11539)
body:
* Keep imported slashing protection from being overwritten by cache

A keymanager import wrote EIP-3076 history to a key's record file, but
the slashing protector kept using the record it had cached for that
key, and wrote values derived from it back over the imported file on
the next signature.

Evict the cached record when a signer is deleted, so a key that is
deleted, run elsewhere and imported again with that history reloads
the imported record. DeletableSigner has drained in-flight signing and
blocks further signing before the eviction runs.

Check for a duplicate key before applying imported slashing protection,
so history sent with a keystore that is already loaded is not applied
and the duplicate response reflects that nothing changed.

fixes #11388

* Stop slashing protection queries from caching records

LocalSlashingProtector.getSigningRecord cached any record it read from
storage. The startup protection summary queues the loaded validators
and queries them later, so a key deleted in between had its pre-delete
record cached again, and a re-import with higher history was then
overwritten on the next signature.

Only the signing path now populates the cache; getSigningRecord reads
storage without caching and is synchronized with the signing methods.

author: Paul Harris
subject: Keep the finalized anchor DAS tracker alive while its payload is recovered (#11553)
body:
* Keep the finalized anchor DAS tracker alive while its payload is recovered

Starting from a state-only Gloas checkpoint, ForkChoice recovers the
anchor's SignedExecutionPayloadEnvelope and runs its data availability
check at the anchor block slot. That slot is always at or below the
finalized epoch start, so DasSamplerBasicImpl.onSlot pruned the sampling
tracker on the next slot tick and completed it exceptionally. The
envelope import then failed with NOT_AVAILABLE and every retry built a
fresh tracker that was pruned the same way.

Exempt the tracker for the latest finalized anchor root from the
finalized-range pruning while data availability is deferred to the
execution payload envelope and the store has no execution payload for
that root. Everything else is pruned as before.

* Pin the anchor tracker exemption to state-only Gloas anchors

Mirror the predicate ForkChoice.onExecutionPayloadEnvelope uses to
recognise a recoverable anchor, resolve the anchor root once per slot
tick and consult the store only on a root match, and log when a
finalized-range tracker is retained. Cover the onExecutionPayloadImported
removal path and pin that pre-Gloas and full anchors never consult the
store.

author: Enrico Del Fante
subject: Close inbound RPC streams whose response cannot be written (#11569)
body:
* Close inbound RPC streams whose response cannot be written

A response or error-response write that fails, or a half-close that
fails, now closes the stream abruptly instead of leaving it half-closed
or open.

Over QUIC a requester that cancels its request closes with FIN plus
STOP_SENDING. After STOP_SENDING quiche refuses every further write,
including our FIN, so netty can never auto-close the stream (it needs
both FINs) and the jvm-libp2p half-close becomes a no-op. The stream
therefore stayed open until the peer disconnected, holding one of the
node-wide 128 inbound RPC stream permits. A single peer cancelling
enough requests exhausted the limit and every other peer's status,
ping, metadata and by-range requests were rejected until that peer left,
which is what took a Hoodi supernode offline for RPC three times in a
day.

The by-range success path was already safe because its write failures
reach completeWithUnexpectedError, which closes abruptly; the
single-response handlers and every error response were not.

* Extract the half-close helper in RpcResponseCallback

Review follow-up: the "half-close, close fully if that fails" step is
now one private closeWriteStream() used from the success path, the
error-response path and completeSuccessfully, instead of the
error-response path calling completeSuccessfully.

author: Enrico Del Fante
subject: Inbound rpc stream backstops (#11578)
body:
* Bound how long inbound RPC streams can hold their permits

A peer could stop the node from serving req/resp by leaving inbound
streams open: a stream only released its slot in the node-wide limit of
128 once fully closed, which the peer controls.

- Cap a single peer at 16 of the 128 inbound stream permits.
- Close an inbound stream still open two minutes after it started.
- Once we half-close an inbound stream, shorten that deadline to five
  seconds, so a stream the peer or transport never finishes is closed.
- The deadline runs on the stream's event loop, so cancelling it on close
  removes the task instead of keeping the stream reachable until it would
  have fired.
- Add rpc_inbound_streams_active, rpc_inbound_streams_rejected_total and
  rpc_inbound_streams_expired_total.

* Handle a shut-down event loop when shortening an inbound stream deadline

- Catch the RejectedExecutionException a terminated event loop throws
  when the half-close hands it the deadline change, so closeWriteStream
  no longer fails and logs an error during shutdown.
- Test that the deadline change waits for the event loop, and that a
  half-close completes when the event loop has shut down.
- Reword the CHANGELOG entry and the lifetime javadoc to match what the
  deadlines do.
- Mark the per-peer active stream accessor as test-only.

* Log inbound RPC stream state on deadline expiry and bound the half-close

The inbound stream deadline log line now names the protocol, which deadline
fired, the stream age and whether the request was received, our half-close
was requested and completed, and the peer's FIN arrived. That tells a FIN
stuck in the QUIC write queue apart from a request never answered.

The half-close after a response is now bounded by RESPONSE_WRITE_TIMEOUT like
a write; if our FIN does not get out in time the stream is closed.

author: Paul Harris
subject: Remove the compromised eMudhra roots from the Docker images (#11577)
body:
* Remove the compromised eMudhra roots from the Docker images

The eMudhra intermediate CAs whose keys were compromised in October
2026 chain to emSign ECC Root CA - G3 and are cross-signed by AAA
Certificate Services. The Eclipse Temurin base images still trust
emSign ECC Root CA - G3, and Java does not check revocation by
default, so the Teku images accept certificates signed with those
keys.

Remove both roots from the jlinked runtime's cacerts in the jdk25 and
jdk26 images. Match them by SHA-256 fingerprint rather than alias, and
fail the build if either is still present, so a renamed alias cannot
silently leave one in place. The step does nothing once the base image
drops them.

* Also remove the emSign Root CA G1 and G2 roots from Docker images

OpenJDK's fix for the eMudhra compromise removes four roots: emSign
ECC Root CA - G3, emSign Root CA - G1, emSign Root CA - G2 and AAA
Certificate Services. Match that list. The Temurin base images ship
emSign Root CA - G1, so this removes it as well as G3; G2 is not in
Temurin and the step does nothing for it.

Temurin's trust store follows Mozilla, which still trusts emSign Root
CA - G1, so unlike the others its removal will not become a no-op when
the base images are updated.

* Announce the upcoming removal of the jdk26 Docker images

Java 26 is end of life and no longer receives security fixes, so the -jdk26 images will stop being published in a future release. Point users at the -jdk25 tags.

author: Gabriel Fukushima
subject: Reject RPC data column sidecars whose fork digest doesn't match their slot fork (#11575)
body:
* Reject RPC data column sidecars whose fork digest does not match their slot

The response decoder picked the SSZ schema from the peer's fork digest
alone, so a peer could label a Gloas-slot sidecar with the Fulu digest and
have it decoded as a Fulu sidecar. Validation then dispatched by slot,
where the Gloas rules skip the inclusion proof, and the commitments
provider trusted the commitments embedded in the sidecar, so sender-chosen
cells verified against sender-chosen commitments and the column was
accepted into custody and the sampling tracker.

- RpcContextCodec gains verifyPayloadMatchesContext, called by
  RpcResponseDecoder after each decoded payload. The fork-digest codec
  rejects a chunk whose digest names a fork other than the one active at
  the payload's slot with the new, penalised ContextPayloadMismatchException.
  ForkDigestPayloadContext.rejectsContextSlotMismatch enables the check per
  payload type; only data column sidecars enable it, so blocks, blob
  sidecars and envelopes keep their behaviour at fork boundaries.
- MiscHelpersGloas.verifyDataColumnSidecar rejects sidecars that are not
  Gloas sidecars.
- BlobKzgCommitmentsProvider ignores commitments carried by a sidecar at a
  Gloas or later slot and resolves them by block root instead.

* Consolidate changelog entry for data column sidecar RPC context handling

* address feedback

Compare against our own encoding in the codec. It now checks the chunk’s digest equals encodeContext(payload), which is stricter (a different BPO digest within the same milestone is rejected), drops the duplicate milestone lookup, and removes the unreachable unknown-digest branch. The codec test covers both fork directions, a same-milestone different digest, and block tolerance.
Recovery task trust gap. “Which commitments does a sidecar carry that we may trust” is now a fork-aware method on the sidecar util, returning the sidecar’s own for Fulu and empty for Gloas. Both the provider and the EL manager’s createRecoveryTask use it, so recovery can no longer use sender-chosen commitments either. A Gloas EL manager test feeds a Fulu-schema sidecar and checks the task waits for the block.
Fulu fails closed like Gloas: verifyDataColumnSidecar returns false for a non-Fulu sidecar instead of throwing, with a test.
Multi-chunk decoder test: a valid chunk followed by a mislabelled one in a single buffer throws and yields nothing.
Nits: final loop variables, assertThatSafeFuture instead of join in the provider tests, PR link on the changelog entry.

Signed-off-by: Gabriel Fukushima <gabrielfukushima@gmail.com>

author: Enrico Del Fante
subject: Bound RocksDB range seeks and skip pruned data column slots (#11585)
body:
* Bound RocksDB range seeks and skip pruned data column slots

Ranged RocksDB streams applied the end of the range only as a Java
predicate, so a seek into a pruned range stepped over every deletion
tombstone up to the first live key. On Sepolia, by-range data column
requests for long-pruned slots took minutes and filled all RPC storage
throttle slots.

- Give ranged stream/streamKeys iterators an exclusive
  iterate_upper_bound; the iterator owns and closes its ReadOptions and
  bound Slice.
- Start streamDataColumnIdentifiers above the prune watermark and skip
  the database when the range is fully pruned.
- Drop sidecar writes at or below the prune watermark.
- Merge RocksDbKeyIterator into a generic RocksDbIterator.

Fixes #11584

* Remove the prune watermark check from addSidecar

No write path stores a data column sidecar at or below the prune
watermark: the pruner cuts more than an epoch below the custody backfill
lower bound, and gossip and sync writes are near the head. The check
added a database read to every sidecar write without closing the race
it targeted, so drop it.

* Simplify bounded RocksDB streams and the prune watermark clamp

- streamDataColumnIdentifiers is now the only place that resumes above
  the prune watermark; the pruner no longer computes it separately.
- Create every RocksDB iterator through one path that always uses
  ReadOptions and only attaches the upper bound for ranged streams, so
  unbounded streams get the same cleanup on failure.
- Tidy the tests: run the pruner tests through the real clamp,
  parameterize the clamp cases, and merge the stream/streamKeys pairs.

* Add changelog entry for pruned data column range seeks

author: Enrico Del Fante
subject: Accumulate decoded snappy frames into a single buffer (#11587)
body:
* Accumulate decoded snappy frames into a single buffer

SnappyFramedDecompressor now copies each decoded frame into one growable
buffer sized from the advertised payload length, instead of retaining
every frame and summing their sizes after each one. Per-frame work is
constant and each frame is released as soon as it is copied.

Eth2OutgoingRequestHandler now releases its response decoder in
closed(), which runs on the stream's event loop, rather than in
abortRequest(), which may run on the timeout thread. The threading
contract is documented on RpcRequestHandler.

* Start the decoded payload buffer empty

Allocate the decoded payload buffer as frames arrive instead of reserving
up to 1 MiB from the advertised length before any data is received. Growth
is still capped at the advertised length, so the final buffer is the same
size.

author: Enrico Del Fante
subject: Compute snappy frame checksums with bulk CRC32C updates (#11593)
body: SnappyUtil.calculateChecksum fed CRC32C one byte at a time, which dominated ssz_snappy RPC decoding: about 5 ms per MB of payload. It now passes the buffer's NIO views to CRC32C.update(ByteBuffer), one per component for composite buffers, so the JDK intrinsic computes it in about 0.1 ms per MB. Decoding a 1 MB payload drops from 3.5 ms to 0.17 ms for incompressible data and from 3.9 ms to 0.65 ms for 2:1 compressible data.
